summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,340.53 on Nov 17 (-1.03%), its fourth straight loss and a five-month low, sitting right on its 200-day average (~7,330) with all 11 sectors red and software leading the drop. NVDA then beat after the close ($115.8B revenue vs ~$109B, Q4 guide $130B vs ~$125B, +$150B buyback) and futures bounced, but the Dow faded intraday on Nov 18, so the beat has not yet repaired the tape. Fragility is up: VIX jumped to ~23–26 (from ~19.3 on Nov 13) with a flat term structure (VIX3M/VIX ≈ 1.00), 200-day breadth slipped to ~56%, and a Dec 9 hike is ~95% priced with Waller still floating 50bp. The one calm signal is credit (HY OAS ~3.20%, tighter than early November). Hold new cash until the S&P either reclaims ~7,500 or October PCE (Nov 25) comes in benign; a daily close below ~7,300 would confirm the 200-day break.
